# Dishwasher Leak During Drain Cycle: Vancouver Renter Repair Brief

The leak pattern points to a **drain-side issue** rather than a constant supply leak. Since it happens **only at the bottom during draining** on a **2019 Bosch** in a rental apartment, the most likely causes are a clogged drain path, a failing pump seal, or a loose hose connection.

## Troubleshooting Checklist for a Bottom Leak

| Step | Action | What to Check | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Run one short cycle and watch the base | Leak appears only when the machine starts pumping out water | Confirms drain-cycle-related leak |
| 2 | Check under the sink | Drain hose connection, clamp, and air gap if present | No drips, loose fittings, or wet cabinet floor |
| 3 | Inspect the dishwasher filter | Food debris, glass, grease buildup | Filter is clean and seated properly |
| 4 | Look at the drain hose path | Kinks, cracks, sagging, or rubbing points | Hose is intact and routed smoothly |
| 5 | Listen during drain | Grinding, rattling, or loud pump noise | May indicate pump obstruction or seal wear |
| 6 | Check for water at front toe-kick/base | Water pooling only when draining | Supports internal drain pump or hose leak |
| 7 | Stop use if leak is active | Protect flooring and cabinets | Prevents further damage |

## Most Likely Causes, Ranked

| Likelihood | Possible cause | Why it fits this symptom | Typical repair |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Clogged filter or drain path | Drain cycle forces water through a restricted path, which can push water out at the base | Clean filter, sump, and drain line |
| 2 | Loose or cracked drain hose connection | Leaks often show only when water is pumped out under pressure | Tighten clamp or replace hose |
| 3 | Failing drain pump seal | Water escapes only when the pump runs | Replace pump seal or pump assembly |
| 4 | Cracked drain hose | Pressure during draining exposes a split that may not leak otherwise | Replace hose |
| 5 | Air gap or sink connection issue | Backflow or overflow at the connection can show up during drain | Clear blockage, reseat connection |
| 6 | Internal sump or tub seal leak | Water reaches the bottom pan during drain surge | Replace seal or related part |
| 7 | Less likely: door seal issue | Usually leaks during wash, not just drain | Inspect only if other causes are ruled out |

## Photos and Notes to Collect

- Photo of the **front bottom/kick plate area** showing any pooled water
- Photo of the **under-sink plumbing** where the drain hose connects
- Photo of the **dishwasher model label** showing brand, model number, and serial number
- Photo of the **filter area** with the rack removed
- Short video of the leak **while the drain cycle runs**
- Note the **exact time** the leak starts: “only when draining,” “after 5 minutes,” etc.
- Note whether there is **any error code, unusual noise, or smell**
- Note whether the leak is **clear water or dirty water**
- Note whether the machine is **built-in, under-counter, and accessible from the front**
- Note if the **floor/cabinet base** is wet or if water appears only in the dishwasher base pan

## Message You Can Send to the Landlord

Hi [Landlord Name],

I wanted to report a dishwasher issue in the apartment. The dishwasher appears to be leaking from the bottom **only during the drain cycle**, not continuously. It is a **2019 Bosch model** in the 2-bedroom unit.

Based on the leak pattern, it may be related to the drain pump, drain hose, or a blockage in the drain path. I have not forced any repairs myself. I can provide photos/video of the leak, the model label, and the under-sink connections if helpful.

Please let me know the next step for scheduling a repair technician.

Thank you,
[Your Name]
